author: someone else
subject: I didn't ask for this (Part 3)
body:
After an hour and a half of him chasing me with no satisfaction, it was time to send him another tell. "tell Jolinne tell G Lol yah it doesn't matter if he is morphed or invis, the bot will never let itself be caught it will keep him busy forever haha". 
With that tell I hoped to make him think I was a bot so that I would 1. Not have any valuable items on me so he would stop with the swap bs, and 2. There was no point in chasing me. In reality, if he caught me while I wasn't paying attention he could actually possibly fuck me up before I could elusion or rescue/blink/run. The conundrum for him, mind you, is that I'm a white name who stays Anonymity'd, so he can't just dispel illusion or he would have to become a criminal to attack me. Not that I doubt he would if he thought he could get away with it, I assess that his psychotic mind is capable of ignoring consequences to satisfy his carnal lust for griefing.
But it wasn't enough, I needed to stoke his paranoia more. A few minutes later I sent a simple broadcast: "Hey mark if ur on we need you to cast hunt again until craig gets his mule up". There is, of course, no Mark or Craig. My intent with that message was to 1. Expand the theater of shadows stalking his psyche through the dark twisted streets of his paranoid mind and 2. Make him think I *also* had access to Hunt mules to actively dissuade him and/or his alts from hunting me. After all, just some bot is not worth his time. Especially if its hyper-advanced technology handforged in the fires of hell by the legion of doom are programmed not to let him catch it. For what it's worth, it appears to have worked as I spent the next two hours farming unbothered. 
What happens next? I dunno, but as much fun as it's been, my moral compass tells me I need to put a stop to this before the next "innocent"-ish player catches a stray harpoon. I hope this has been a lesson for everyone. Or someone. 
In the meanwhile, I remain logged in as much as I can and have since diverted my efforts into a different character who shall remain nameless and unknown. Or maybe I haven't? Maybe I'm still only on the one character as I always have been? Who's to say. I'm sure he'll find his man eventually though. There's someone for everyone.

author: Unknown Caller
subject: I didn't ask for this (Part 2)
body:
Jolinne (Jorval), ecstatic to receive this accidental tidbit of intelligence from one of his enemies, goes on to proclaim with joy in broadcast chat that his fears have been validated. There IS a secret organization stalking him, cavorting and in cahoots with one another plotting his downfall and the destruction of the server's innocence. Is there really? Fuck if I know, but at least he has someone else to bother now.
Could I have spent the time to painstakingly explain that no, I'm not a bot and no,  I don't have anything to do with whoever the fuck Akiros is? Yes, yes I could have. Did I? Nope. 
I sent another anonymous tell minutes later to Jolinne along the lines of "tell Jolinne tell S fix your shitty tell macro man" (There was no one online who's name started with S at the time). About five minutes later I also sent another anonymous broadcast begging to be let back into a discord server they were supposedly banned from for making a "mistake". I would later realize that these accoutrements to my subterfuge were wholly unnessary as I was simply throwing more pearls of evidence before swine.
Now back to Jorval's fears that have been realized. There's now at least one or more secret rings of PKers and one of them is a spy. He's got an inside man to deal with now. A mole to hunt. I can get back to building in peace now I think to myself. 
Days go by, his stoked paranoia escalating into a raging firestorm of outrage and finger pointing on the adventure globes. Witch hunts abound as he mulls over that one glaring piece of evidence which has been presented to him on a silver platter: Who was "G"? Surely this letter was some important fulcrum of the investigation that would lead to a breakthrough! G must mean someone important! It must mean Gar!  (Sorry Gar, I didn't see that one coming). After all, a big important server celebrity guild leader Gaston hyper-chad whom fights daily to slog through the veritable sea of girl's panties being thrown at them to shitpost at the adventurer's hall must need a big important arch nemesis! It couldn't be that intelligence given to you by your enemy might be total bullshit! *Cough* Akiros *Cough*...
My days of pleasant unbothered grinding continued for a while. I stocked Rook's chest with extra plates, helmets, circlets, spell school robes etc. I gain another 25hp and fill my bank with delicious reagents while popping into crypts occasionally to buff newbs and plop gifts. I even work up my unnecessary spells. I might even eventually become a coveted adventurer statue. Life goals amirite?!
But no, about a week later and I've got him on my ass again.  I had become his white whale, his sole focus that became the itch that he must scratch. Blinded out of nowhere as I stepped out of Marion to practice my bard spells, I became the victim of Swap as my coveted wrought iron key was replaced by one of his disgustingly skin-tight black patrick swayze t-shirts. The horror. Clutching my pearls, I ducked backwards into Marion and Elusioned away to the island to restock my reagents at the bank. Stepping out, there he was yet again staring at me in the street like he knew I was in there, squatting in the sprint starting position like a sex offender in a San Francisco park.
I elusioned back to my room at the Inn to go make a cup ramen and when I got back I noticed a message I had never seen before: "You have somehow managed to shake off your trackers!" Oh. Oh Fuck. This asshole has HUNT mules. Jesus christ. He wasn't going to leave me alone! Well fuck it then lets see how bad he wants it. 
For almost two hours  I watch his impotent little blue dot chasing me through towns, through caves, through every turn of the jungle. It was titilating, this game of cat and mouse we shared. I matched my morphs to the creatures of the land and watched him pass right by me as I ran the other way after his back was turned. Rescue potions, invisibility rings, elusioning so much it would have been dangerous for an epileptic. I was getting so titilated that my nipples could cut glass.

author: Unknown Caller
subject: I didn't ask for this (Part 1)
body:
"There's someone for everyone." That's what I chuckled to myself when I made my character. Originally I had named him "Someone" before thinking better of it and changing it to "someone".  I wanted there to remain a clear distiction from tells sent to/by "someone" and the "Someone" people see when using anonymity. I figured "Someone" was a no-go, but thought that since "someone" is mechanically different in every important aspect in regards to game functions the GMs would let it slide. Which they seem to have. 
I don't make a big footprint. I'm an old player. Old old. (40's+). I never did a lot of pvp. I never joined a guild. I have fun running around in the background getting stronger and helping out new players, all while constantly keeping up some combination of anonymity/shadow form/morph. If you've ever been fully buffed by a ghost in crypts or were dropped a stack of Inkys in the inn by a baby spider, that may have been me. I don't say anything. When people send tells to "someone" by mistake, I quickly cast dispel illusion and respond like I have no idea what's going on before recasting Anonymity and pretending I didn't see a thing as I continue to provide information or answer questions in broadcast chat. 
I don't usually read the adventure hall globes very often, but I do every once in a while if there's some sort of server drama going on. A character called "Jolinne" starting calling me "Akiros's bot" and I had no idea who either of these people were. I'm no one's alt, and I'm not a bot so this noticeably raised one of my eyebrows. I run to the adventure globes to discover that indeed, someone named "Akiros" apparently "accidentally divulged" my name as one of his alts. He said some nonsense about having a new Riija 6 character and when asked for a name replied "someone lol". Fuck me right? I don't want to have to explain I'm not a bot. I shouldn't have to, that's not my job. Plus, would he even believe me if I did?
So soon after that I'm farming orc teeth in Icky like normal and notice a *possibly mule* char standing by the chalice of the rain. I think nothing of it until Jolinne comes flying at me through the cave 30 seconds later, her sword harmlessly bouncing off of my gold round shield as I duck out the entrance and elusion away. I'm like "Well this is annoying, apparently he/she has bots watching popular spots for me. I'm just trying to get to 150hp and amass a mountain of shillings before I get bored and have to decide if I want to turn into a crazy murderer like a normal person. But no, I had to get dragged into this stupid server drama and now Jolinne broadcasts about me "He has "for everyone" in his bio but what he doesn't realize is that a friend to everyone is a friend to none!". Okay great, I think to myself, I'm dealing with a gullible crazy moron.
So anyways, here's where I probably start to become the bad guy... 
I don't pvp a lot, nor do I want to. But one thing I do have is a very particular set of skills. Skills acquired over a very long career playing MMO's and shitposting that make me a nightmare for gullible people with paranoia. Psychological warfare it is then.
I do a quick /who to see there is a ton of people on. I look for the letter that begins the most player names. There were 4 players online whose names started with a G (and for the record NONE of them were Gar). I refresh my anonymity with a dispel illusion as I crack my knuckles in my cozy room at The Aerie Guest House. I send Jolinne a message to test the waters of his paranoia (I know it's a He by now from reading the globes): "tell Jolinne tell G No not yet, he can't know you're with us." Someone used Psychological Warfare. It was super effective.

author: Hell
subject: How Meridian 59 REALLY Got Its Name
body:
Originally, Meridian 59 was supposed to have a much simpler name: Meridian. Clean. Mysterious. Elegant.

There was only one problem. The name Meridian had already been trademarked by a completely unrelated company that made printer software and drivers. Yes.A printer company. 

Imagine creating an enormous online fantasy world full of monsters, magic, adventure, and players trying to murder each other only to discover that your greatest enemy isn't a dragon but a printer.

So the developers needed a new name. Fortunately, it was 1995, and Windows 95 was everywhere. The game was heading toward its December 1995 release, so someone supposedly looked at "95" and had a moment of inspiration: "What if we just flip it?"

95 became 59... And thus... Meridian became Meridian 59. Meridian 59 was released in December 1995.

Which means that if development had slipped by just one more month, the game would have arrived in 1996. And naturally, following exactly the same naming system...

96 would have become 69.... Ladies and gentlemen: MERIDIAN 69. 

Perhaps December 1995 didn't just give us Meridian 59. Perhaps it saved the franchise.

author: Hell
subject: Lessons for the Newly Arrived
body:
To those newly arrived in Meridian: do not measure progress only by what you can kill. Learn the roads, exits, merchants, and places where running is wiser than fighting. Carry only what you can afford to lose, and spend your gold before greed gives someone else the chance to take it. 

Learn which creatures you can defeat, but more importantly, learn which ones you should simply walk around. Ask questions. Meridian is old, and much of what matters is never explained. Do not neglect your skills just because a new spell or weapon looks more exciting. A powerful ability you cannot use well is just expensive decoration.

Do not fill your inventory with things you are afraid to lose. Bring what you need for the trip and leave unnecessary valuables somewhere safe. A little preparation can save far more gold than a little extra courage.

Pay attention to your health, mana, vigor, reagents, food, and equipment before entering a dangerous area. If one of them is already running low, the dungeon will not improve the situation. There is no shame in returning to town early. The corpse on the floor usually belonged to someone who wanted "just one more kill."

Learn landmarks instead of relying entirely on memory. Doors, bridges, unusual rooms, statues, stairways, and intersections can become your compass when everything starts looking the same. When entering somewhere unfamiliar, occasionally turn around and look behind you the path home often looks completely different from the other direction.

Most importantly, do not rush because another player appears stronger or richer than you. Meridian rewards knowledge slowly and punishes impatience quickly. Every trip should teach you something, even if all you bring home is the knowledge of where not to go next time. A prepared adventurer may not look impressive leaving town, but he usually looks much better returning to it.

 Hell, Meridian's Luminary Wanderer

Here is the assumption many of us had pre-open source. I guess we could dig to find the answer these days.

Councilors can be shifted +1 or +2 based meeting their requirements. An unfactioned councilor would go to weak with +1 or strong with +2. To go from strong to dedicated, you'd want to only move them +1. If you oversold the faction by going +2, they'd eventually wander from dedicated to unfactioned again. 

If they were already on dedicated, you would definitely shift them by turning in a token to them, so you'd turn it into your faction leader instead to avoid overinfluence. 

This could all just be a silly assumption, but we were always careful not to overshift a councilor.

author: Holigan
subject: Goodbye
body:
Well, the time has finally come. 

This will be my final term as your Royal Justicar. 

I've had the privilege of serving this server for three terms, and I can honestly say I've learned a lot, made plenty of friends, made a few enemies, and apparently became the villain in some people's stories. That's just part of the job. 

To those who supported me from day one, thank you. Your trust meant more than you know. To those who couldn't stand seeing my name as Justicar... congratulations, your wish is finally coming true. 

Whether you agreed with my decisions or not, every ruling I made was with the intention of doing what I believed was best for the server and not just for my wallet. I wasn't perfect, and I never claimed to be, but I always gave this role my best effort. 

To whoever takes over after me: good luck. You will quickly learn that everyone wants justice, right up until it's their turn to face it.
 
Thank you for the memories, the laughs, the arguments, the late night messages, and even the complaints (best part) they all made this journey memorable. 

As for me, I'll be hanging up the Justicar title and returning to the life of causing problems instead of solving them.



Truly,

The toughest, cutest, and now officially retired warrior of all time.

author: Lauranna
subject: Discord
body:
Discord has brought some good things to Meridian, vis a vis 'the 90s', such as voicechat alongside playing. But it's also brought disadvantages.

Imho the current Discord server is toxic. One of the results of this is people treating Meridian like they do social media in general. Playing under their real life name, interacting with each other in real life terms, not game terms. 

This was never what Meridian was about: we're in a virtual world, not the real world. You don't have to full on roleplay if that's not your thing (but great if it is).

But the whole point is to have an avatar(s) that isn't real life; to play and live in the virtual world as the character(s) you create.

It would be a big step forward if people playing as their 'real life self', complete with banners shouting their real life name, would consider the setting, and save 'social media' for, well, social media.

This is a game to play and have fun, it's not a popularity contest or a way to tell everyone how great you are.

Thank you for your attention on this matter.

Just to re-itterate: anyone who wants 'out' from being hunted as part of the pkers guild Kalior's Elite/ Mostly Americans / All Americans:

All you have to do is leave the guild and ally yourself with a different guild, or none. Just make a post on the globe to say you've left and you will no longer be hunted.

The reason these players are curerntly being hunted is simple: 

They are a group of veterans with many fully-built characters, who between them run around 10 red pkers.

This group of players uses a 'war between friends' as a way to supposedly support the server and introduce 'new players' to pvp.

In reality, this means that anyone in the war has to play by certain agreed rules, and the result is that their red pkers get free reign to attack innocent newer players whenever they feel like it.

Some of these red pkers and shield pkers include: Bloody Dreams, Bloody Dreams Eleven, Zadok, Jabberwocky, Churl, Hosni Mubarak, Luz de Sol.

Although not everyone in the guild pks randomly like these people, the 'cover' of the 'friends guild war' means that if anyone was to attack and log one of the pker characters, then the *whole* guild, with mutiple characters per driver, will come to their aid. Normally this means the red named or shield pker is able to log back on without consequence.

It also means that anyone who doesn't play by their rules, or does anything they don't like (and this can be really petty, like saying "do you want some cheese with your whine"?) will get hunted by their red pkers and other guild members, ferociously.

Realistically, the bulk of players who enjoy pvp and fight in the 'friendly war' who are 'hunters' (the guild 'Infernal Machine'), will only do so much to hunt the pker characters, because if they log them, they will then have to face multiple built 'halo' characters (white characters in the guild war who can attack their rival guild without going coloured).

The net result is that the 10 or so coloured pkers and 'shield pkers' most of the time have nobody hunting them. Most of the time these characters don't go out killing innocents. But when the 'friendly war' is quiet, they cannot resist going out and pking to get their pvp fix.

The result of this was in the last few months, two genuine new players who were giving the game serious consideration together, were driven away because basically they got pk'd too many times- and by the characters named above. I confirmed this independently, out of game, including the names.

body:
If you are using the Steam client...you can't. Or rather, you can't use the steam client for more than one at a time.

You *can* run the Steam client, then make a new 2nd account, and download the web client from Meridian59.com -- as far as I know you can also open 2 of the web client.

Only three characters can be logged in from the same IP address regardess, so that can throttle things.

I had to completely uninstall my steam client, then install the web client and get it working, then reinstall the steam client to be able to run one instance of each client for my 2 accounts.

author: Aeorsk
subject: Re: info
body:
There's nothing out there that's really modern.  I believe most people still go to the "Gilroy's" website, though I believe the original owner took it down, but handed it over to the M59 team.

Quick guide on stats:
Hidden stats: Offense and Defense, your chance to hit and evade attacks.  Cap is 1000.  1000 Offense against 1000 defense = 50% chance to hit.

Might: 1 pt = 20 burden, 1 burden = 1 emerald, you start with 1700 base.  Anything over 25 adds 1% melee damage, up to 40% max at 65 Might

Intellect: Every 5 points gives you 1 more level of a school to learn, you start with the ability to learn level 6 in one and level 4 in another (6/4), so 5 intellect will let you do 6/5 and 10 intellect 6/6.  Riija / Jala softcaps

Stamina: Increases HP regen (there's a cap that usually is hit easily past 100HP), and allows for max HP past 100.  Each max HP gives 1.5 Offense and 1.5 Defense.  Kraanan softcap

Agility: Increases Defense by 4 per point, used in Disarm calculations, should aim for at least 20 if you're getting it. Disarm is Weaponcraft 6, it stuns mobs and knocks weapons out of hands of players.  Once its 99%, Agility doesn't really matter.

Mysticism: Increases base mana, mana per node and mana regen.  Goes by 5 and then 10s, so 5myst equals a bonus, then 15, then 25, etc.  Most use a rose that gives a longterm 5 Myst buff and go for either 40 or 50 Mysticism.  Needed at a high amount if you plan to do any casting.  30 Myst + Rose + all nodes + circlet will let you reach max regen (circlet trades max HP for max mana while worn)

Aim: Increases offense by 4 per point, anything past 25 increases archery damage by 1% to a max of 40% at 65 Aim (only 60 Aim is possible with Jonas shield + Monocle)

2-school pure fighter, generally suggested to build first.
39 Might / 10 Int / 50 Stam / 50 Agil / 1 Myst / 50 Aim
My preferred PF, as with SS and Jonas shield you're at 64 Might. 6 Kraanan 6 Weaponcraft

3-school Karma build (Qor / Shal)
40 Might / 25 Int / 40 Sta / 10 Agi / 50 Myst / 35 Aim
6WC / 5Kraanan / 5 Shal
Tweak however, if you really like bow for example you can do 39/20/40/1/50/50 to get aim to 50.

Pure casters go 48/50/50/1/50/1, you need to carry a lot of junk.

Recommended you get Kraanan 3 ASAP in any build. Bless increases your damage and adds 100 Offense, Magic Shield adds 250 Defense.  Kraanan.  Always take ATLEAST Weaponcraft 2 in any build, Dodge adds 297 Defense and Block adds 99, Parry is 198.

Kraanan = Buffs
Qor = CC / Damage
Shal'ille = heals / CC / undead damage / buffs (umbrella 250 Defense & damage reduct vs undead, forces of light bonus offense/dmg vs evil)
Faren = elemental damage (touch of flame / fireball / firewall) / spiderweb CC
Jala = area buffs / debuffs (the debuffs are crap except Jig) and a super mint to restore all your mana at 6.  Usually just a bot / 2nd account runs it
Riija = Debuffs / illusionary clones / morph / teleport / much more; very powerful but costly to build.  Not recommended for a new build

author: Ihsan
subject: Re: Aw: Money farm
body:
For any of this discussion to matter, you'd need to somehow engage the administration in a conversation

For the past several years, they have been quite antagonistic in design toward players making money. Avar warrior farming was nuked, brax/TR was killed, chieftain farming at avar village had some disruptive spawn points added, Roq and Wulfgang had their buy prices cut by 10%. If you farmed 'too much' you would also face live edits to a room's spawn or attributes, or suffer personal repercussions.

This is a fairly common trap that 'green' dev teams fall into. It's hard to get objective data, so what they personally see matters more. What they see is this - they log in invisible. They go to players and watch them. They see someone they already don't quite like (a veteran) farming Avar Village with a complex bait, lightning wall, and mule set up.

Their gut reaction is negative.

So, they live edit, or code nerfs. The reasons they give vary, with all sorts of justifications about balance / newbies vs vets / economy, but really at the end of the day it's just that gut reaction that 'this is wrong' and 'this is abusive of the game engine.' There's no debating past this, since it's not really a logical position. If it was, there would be numbers, metrics, and equations involved. But there aren't. Because it's not.

All we can do is carry on. Play or don't. This situation can't be fixed
